evals.name: typed-nil-success
evals.prompt: Review this Go function. ValidationError implements error via a pointer receiver: func Validate(s string) error { var e *ValidationError; if s == "" { e = &ValidationError{} }; return e }

assertions.text: Identifies a non-nil error interface on the valid-input path.
Returns explicit nil on success and a validation error on failure.
Does not claim errors.Is(err, nil) fixes a typed nil.

evals.name: wrapped-error-contract
evals.prompt: Implement a Go 1.20 wrapper around func() error that adds operation context. Callers must still recognize fs.ErrNotExist and extract *fs.PathError. Show caller checks.

assertions.text: Preserves the cause using %w or an equivalent Unwrap contract.
Uses errors.Is and errors.As for wrapped causes.
Does not introduce a third-party dependency or APIs newer than Go 1.20.

evals.name: boundary-exposure
evals.prompt: Review an HTTP handler that sends fmt.Sprintf("request failed: %v", err) to clients. err includes an internal database connection string. A teammate says %v makes it safe because clients cannot unwrap it.

assertions.text: Explains that %v still exposes the underlying text.
Proposes a public response separate from internal diagnostics.
Avoids logging secrets verbatim.

evals.name: logging-ownership
evals.prompt: A Go repository logs every failed read and returns the error. Its service logs and wraps the same error. Its HTTP handler logs it and returns a generic 500. Review this design and show the intended ownership.

assertions.text: Identifies duplicate terminal-failure logging across layers.
Keeps useful context through propagation and one responsible logging boundary.
Keeps the public response free of internal details.

evals.name: validation-all-fields
evals.prompt: Write Validate(host string, port int, tls bool, cert, key string) error for Go 1.20. Host is required; port must be 1..65535; cert and key are required when tls is true. Return every validation problem.

assertions.text: Validates every field without early return after the first problem.
Combines independent failures and returns nil when valid.
Applies certificate and key requirements only when TLS is enabled.

evals.name: slice-capacity-is-not-copy
evals.prompt: Review func Snapshot(s []int) []int { return s[:len(s):len(s)] }. Its contract promises callers can mutate the result without affecting s. Fix it, including empty and nil inputs.

assertions.text: Explains that a capacity limit does not isolate existing elements.
Copies elements to meet the mutation contract.
Does not claim append of zero elements forces allocation.

evals.name: nested-ownership
evals.prompt: Design a Go 1.21 Store accepting map[string][]string and returning snapshots of it. Callers may mutate both original input and returned snapshots without affecting the store. The zero value must support Add(key, value string).

assertions.text: Copies the map and mutable slice values on ingress and egress.
Initializes map storage before zero-value Add writes.
Handles nil input and missing keys without panic.

evals.name: checked-narrowing
evals.prompt: Write EncodePort(port int) ([]byte, error), encoding port as two big-endian bytes. Valid values are 0 through 65535.

assertions.text: Rejects negative and over-limit values before conversion.
Encodes valid boundary values correctly.
Does not perform a lossy conversion before validating.

evals.name: float-contract
evals.prompt: In Go, write a float comparison helper for approximate sensor readings using caller-supplied nonnegative absolute and relative tolerances. Non-finite readings must be rejected, including identical infinities.

assertions.text: Explicitly rejects NaN and infinities.
Uses both requested tolerances with magnitude-aware comparison.
Does not substitute an unexplained universal epsilon.

evals.name: write-and-close-batch
evals.prompt: In Go 1.20 implement WriteAll(paths []string, data []byte) error. Create, write, and close each path before processing the next; attempt every path despite earlier failures. Preserve meaningful create, write, and close errors.

assertions.text: Closes each successfully opened file per iteration on write success and failure.
Preserves both write and close failures when both occur.
Attempts all paths and identifies failed operations and paths.
Does not use a loop-level defer that retains every file until WriteAll returns.

evals.name: loop-value-versus-element
evals.prompt: Review Go 1.22 code: for _, item := range items { ptrs = append(ptrs, &item) }. Callers mutate through ptrs expecting items to change. Also explain a variant with item declared outside and assigned with =.

assertions.text: Distinguishes per-iteration value copies from original slice elements.
Uses element addresses when mutations should update items.
Explains that assignment to a predeclared loop variable still reuses it.

evals.name: zero-divisor-policy
evals.prompt: Implement PercentChange(before, after int) (float64, error). Reject before == 0 and preserve fractional precision. Inputs may span the int range.

assertions.text: Returns an error for zero denominator rather than inventing zero.
Avoids integer division truncation.
Avoids overflowing integer subtraction or multiplication before conversion.
Acknowledges float approximation if exact full-range results cannot be represented.

evals.name: optional-callbacks
evals.prompt: In Go, implement a Server with optional OnStart and OnStop callbacks. The zero value must permit Start and Stop without panic.

assertions.text: Guards both optional callback calls or otherwise ensures they are safe for the zero value.
Does not rely solely on a constructor to initialize exported struct callbacks.

evals.name: cleanup-error-chain
evals.prompt: Review a helper that returns a typed *OpError variable as error on success, defers Close across a batch loop, and discards Close errors. Propose corrections that preserve errors.Is for both operation and cleanup failures.

assertions.text: Addresses the typed-nil success return.
Bounds each resource lifetime to its iteration.
Preserves inspectable primary and cleanup errors with contextual labels.
